Banach adjoint duality therefore gives \(R_p=R_{p'}\). Testing Taylor truncations of the disk automorphism \(\phi_a(z)=(a-z)/(1-az)\) on a far basis vector produces disjoint coordinates and exactly the stated powered coefficient sum, yielding the \( eta_q\) upper bound. The endpoint \(\ell_1\) and \(\ell_\infty\) norms reduce exactly to the classical Bohr sum, while \(p=2\) is von Neumann's inequality. The two first-order expansions around \(q=2\) correctly bracket the linear defect by \((\log2)/2\) and \((\log3)/2\).
